questions.questionText: Given that √3 is irrational, prove that (5 + 2√3) is an irrational number.
questions.correctAnswer: Assume 5 + 2√3 = a/b (where a, b are coprime integers, b ≠ 0). 2√3 = a/b - 5 => √3 = (a - 5b)/2b. RHS is rational, which contradicts that √3 is irrational.

questions.questionText: Find the zeros of the quadratic polynomial p(x) = 6x² - 3 - 7x and verify the relationship between zeros and coefficients.
Find the coordinates of a point A, where AB is the diameter of a circle whose center is (2, -3) and B is (1, 4).
questions.correctAnswer: Let A = (x, y). Center is midpoint: (x+1)/2 = 2 => x = 3; (y+4)/2 = -3 => y = -10. Point A is (3, -10).

questions.questionText: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeros are (3 + √5) and (3 - √5).
questions.correctAnswer:
Sum of zeros (S) = (3 + √5) + (3 - √5) = 6.
Product of zeros (P) = (3 + √5)(3 - √5) = 3² - (√5)² = 9 - 5 = 4.
Required polynomial p(x) = k(x² - Sx + P) = k(x² - 6x + 4).
questions.markingScheme:

questions.questionText: Find the 20th term from the last term of the AP: 3, 8, 13, ..., 253.
questions.correctAnswer:
Reversing the AP gives first term A = 253, common difference D = -5.
20th term = A + 19D = 253 + 19(-5) = 253 - 95 = 158.

questions.questionText: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. Find the probability of getting: (i) A black king (ii) A red face card.

(i) Black kings = 2. P = 2/52 = 1/26.

questions.questionText: If sin (A - B) = 1/2 and cos (A + B) = 1/2, where 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find values of A and B.
questions.correctAnswer: A - B = 30° and A + B = 60°. Adding both gives 2A = 90° => A = 45°, B = 15°.

questions.questionText: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin θ - 2 sin³ θ) / (2 cos³ θ - cos θ) = tan θ.
questions.correctAnswer:
LHS = [sin θ (1 - 2 sin² θ)] / [cos θ (2 cos² θ - 1)].
Since 1 - 2 sin² θ = cos 2θ and 2 cos² θ - 1 = cos 2θ (or replacing 1 = sin² θ + cos² θ), numerator and denominator brackets cancel out: sin θ / cos θ = tan θ = RHS.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the cable tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.correctAnswer: Let height of tower = H = CE + ED. Building AB = 7 m => ED = 7 m. In △ABD, tan 45° = AB/BD = 7/BD => BD = 7 m = AE. In △CAE, tan 60° = CE/AE = CE/7 = √3 => CE = 7√3 m. Total height H = 7 + 7√3 = 7(1 + 1.732) = 19.124 m.

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side.
questions.questionText:
Read the passage above and answer the following questions:
Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.

[1 Mark] m = -1 calculation

questions.casePassage: A domestic electric circuit is supplied with 220 V alternating current (AC) with a 50 Hz frequency. In an urban household, appliances such as an electric iron (1100 W), a refrigerator (400 W), four LED bulbs (25 W each), and a television (100 W) are connected across a 15 A power line through safety devices including an MCB and earth wire.
questions.questionText:
Q1. Why are domestic electrical appliances connected in parallel combination rather than series? (1M)
Q2. Calculate the total electric current drawn when all the above appliances operate simultaneously on 220 V. (2M)

questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Parallel combination ensures each appliance receives full 220 V, operates independently with its own switch, and if one appliance fails, others continue working.
Q2. Total Power P = 1100 + 400 + (4 × 25) + 100 = 1700 W. Total Current I = P/V = 1700 / 220 = 7.73 A.
Q3. Protects circuit from overloading and short-circuits by breaking the circuit when current exceeds safe rating.

questions.casePassage: Gregor Mendel conducted pioneering hybridization experiments on garden pea plants (Pisum sativum). He crossed a pure-breeding round and yellow-seeded pea plant (RRYY) with a pure-breeding wrinkled and green-seeded pea plant (rryy). In the F1 generation, all offspring had round and yellow seeds. The F1 generation plants were then self-pollinated to produce the F2 generation.
questions.questionText:
Q1. What is the genotype and phenotype of the F1 generation plants? (1M)
Q2. State Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment demonstrated by this dihybrid cross. (1M)
Q3. State the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation. If 1600 plants are obtained in F2, calculate the expected number of plants with round and green seeds. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Genotype: RrYy; Phenotype: Round and Yellow seeds.
Q2. When two pairs of contrasting traits are combined in a hybrid, segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair during gamete formation.
Q3. Phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1 (Round-Yellow : Round-Green : Wrinkled-Yellow : Wrinkled-Green). Expected Round-Green = (3/16) × 1600 = 300 plants.

(b) A convex lens has focal length 20 cm in air. Find its focal length when immersed in water (μ_glass = 1.5, μ_water = 4/3).

(b) 1/f_air = (1.5 - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = 0.5 K = 1/20 ⇒ K = 1/10. In water: 1/f_water = (1.5/(4/3) - 1) K = (9/8 - 1)(1/10) = (1/8)(1/10) = 1/80 ⇒ f_water = 80 cm.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between Prudential and Moral reasons for power sharing with suitable examples.

Prudential Reasons: Based on careful calculation of gains and losses. Power sharing reduces the possibility of social conflict and ensures political stability (e.g., reserving seats for minority communities in Belgium).
Moral Reasons: Based on the intrinsic value of democracy. Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy where citizens have a right to be consulted on how they are governed.

questions.questionText: What is decentralisation? Describe the major steps taken in 1992 towards decentralisation in India through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments.
questions.correctAnswer:
Decentralisation means taking power away from Central and State governments and giving it to local government.
Major Steps in 1992:
1. Mandatory regular elections to local government bodies.
2. Reservation of seats for SC, ST, and OBC communities.
3. At least one-third (33%) of all positions reserved for women.
4. Creation of an independent State Election Commission in each state.
5. State governments required to share powers and revenue with local bodies.
questions.markingScheme:

[4 Marks] 4 distinct constitutional provisions post-1992 amendment

questions.questionText: What is Per Capita Income? Why is it inadequate as a sole indicator of human development?
questions.correctAnswer: Per Capita Income = Total National Income / Total Population. It is inadequate because it hides disparities in income distribution and does not reflect access to health, education, and social equity.

questions.questionText: Distinguish between 'Coming Together' and 'Holding Together' federations with one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer:
Coming Together: Independent states come together on their own to form a bigger unit to pool sovereignty and retain identity (e.g., USA, Australia).
Holding Together: A large country divides its power between constituent states and the national government (e.g., India, Spain).

questions.questionText: Solve the following problem regarding various institutional and technological reforms introduced by the Government of India in the agricultural sector after independence.
questions.correctAnswer:
Institutional Reforms:
1. Collectivization, consolidation of land holdings, and abolition of the Zamindari system.
2. Provision of crop insurance against drought, flood, cyclone, fire, and diseases.
3. Establishment of Grameen banks, cooperative societies, and Kisan Credit Card (KCC).
Technological Reforms:
4. Green Revolution using HYV seeds and chemical fertilizers, and White Revolution (Operation Flood).
5. Special weather bulletins and agricultural programs broadcast over radio and television.

questions.questionText: Why is credit considered to have a 'double-edged' impact on borrowers? Explain with contrasting examples.
questions.correctAnswer:
Positive impact: Credit enables profitable investment in farming/business, increasing earnings (e.g., Salim expanding shoe production).
Negative impact (Debt Trap): If crops fail due to natural disasters, repayment becomes impossible, forcing the borrower to sell land (e.g., Swapna's crop failure).

questions.questionText: 'Democracy is seen to be good in principle, but felt to be not so good in its practice.' Critically evaluate this statement.
questions.correctAnswer:
In Principle: Democracy promotes equality, enhances individual dignity, improves decision quality, and provides peaceful mechanisms to resolve social conflicts.
In Practice: Democracies often appear slow due to deliberative procedures, suffer from corruption, and do not eliminate poverty overnight.
Conclusion: Democracy is an enabling political framework that creates conditions for citizens to achieve goals, making it superior to any alternative regime.

questions.casePassage: Sustainable development requires balancing economic progress with environmental preservation. Groundwater in India is under serious threat of overuse in many parts of the country. About 300 districts have reported a water level decline of over 4 meters during the past 20 years. Nearly one-third of the country is overusing its groundwater reserves, particularly in agriculturally prosperous regions of Punjab and Western UP.
questions.questionText:
Q1. Identify two regions in India facing severe groundwater overuse. (1M)
Q2. What percentage of the country is currently overusing its groundwater reserves? (1M)
Q3. Explain why sustainable development is crucial for future generations with reference to groundwater depletion. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh.
Q2. Nearly one-third (33%) of the country.
Q3. Groundwater is a renewable resource, but if extraction exceeds natural recharge by rainfall, it leads to irreversible water scarcity, threatening food security and ecosystem survival.

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side.
questions.questionText:
Read the passage above and answer the following questions:
Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.
questions.markingScheme:
[1 Mark] v = 30 cm with formula
[1 Mark] m = -1 calculation
[2 Marks] Full image formed with explanation of reduced brightness due to half light intensity

questions.casePassage: Power sharing arrangements can take many forms in modern democracies. In Belgium, the Constitution prescribes that the number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers shall be equal in the Central Government. Many powers of the Central Government have been given to State Governments of the two regions. Brussels has a separate government in which both communities have equal representation. This accommodative model prevented civil strife.
questions.questionText:
Q1. What constitutional provision ensured linguistic equality in the Belgian Central Government? (1M)
Q2. How did Brussels address the linguistic division between French and Dutch speakers? (1M)
Q3. Contrast Belgium's model of accommodation with Sri Lanka's policy of Majoritarianism. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers.
Q2. Brussels established a separate government with equal community representation.
Q3. Belgium recognized diversity and shared power equally, whereas Sri Lanka adopted majoritarian policies favoring Sinhala supremacy, which triggered civil war.

generalInstructions: This question paper contains questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. Internal choices are provided in 2 questions of Section C, all questions of Section D, and 1 question of Section E.
Section A comprises Objective Type questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 120 to 150 words.
Section E comprises Case-Based / Source-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts (i), (ii), and (iii).
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat, properly labeled diagrams and step-wise calculations should be shown.

(b) Why is double circulation advantageous in birds and mammals?
(c) Distinguish between arteries and veins based on wall thickness, direction of flow, and internal valves.
questions.correctAnswer:

questions.questionText: An object 4 cm tall is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, nature, and size of the image formed.

u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm.

generalInstructions: This question paper contains questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. Internal choices are provided in 2 questions of Section C, all questions of Section D, and 1 question of Section E.
Section A comprises Objective Type questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 120 to 150 words.
Section E comprises Case-Based / Source-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts (i), (ii), and (iii).
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat, properly labeled diagrams and step-wise calculations should be shown.

questions.correctAnswer: Given circle with center O, external point P, tangents PA and PB. Join OA, OB, OP. In right △OAP and △OBP: OA = OB (radii), OP = OP (common), ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°. △OAP ≅ △OBP (RHS). Therefore, PA = PB (CPCT).

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

questions.questionText:

21x + 47y = 110
47x + 21y = 162
questions.correctAnswer:
Adding: 68x + 68y = 272 => x + y = 4 (Eq 1).
Subtracting: -26x + 26y = -52 => -x + y = -2 => x - y = 2 (Eq 2).
Solving: x = 3, y = 1.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the cable tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.correctAnswer: Let height of tower = H = CE + ED. Building AB = 7 m => ED = 7 m. In △ABD, tan 45° = AB/BD = 7/BD => BD = 7 m = AE. In △CAE, tan 60° = CE/AE = CE/7 = √3 => CE = 7√3 m. Total height H = 7 + 7√3 = 7(1 + 1.732) = 19.124 m.

questions.questionText: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin θ - 2 sin³ θ) / (2 cos³ θ - cos θ) = tan θ.
questions.correctAnswer:
LHS = [sin θ (1 - 2 sin² θ)] / [cos θ (2 cos² θ - 1)].
Since 1 - 2 sin² θ = cos 2θ and 2 cos² θ - 1 = cos 2θ (or replacing 1 = sin² θ + cos² θ), numerator and denominator brackets cancel out: sin θ / cos θ = tan θ = RHS.

questions.questionText: If the sum of the first 7 terms of an AP is 49 and that of first 17 terms is 289, find the sum of first n terms.

(b) In △ABC, DE ∥ BC such that AD/DB = 3/5. If AC = 5.6 cm, find AE.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting other two sides, it divides them in the same ratio. Proof using area ratios of △ADE, △BDE, △CDE.
(b) AE/AC = AD/AB = 3/(3+5) = 3/8 => AE = (3/8) × 5.6 = 2.1 cm.

questions.questionText: From an external point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with center O. If ∠APB = 80°, then ∠POA is:

questions.questionText:
Read the passage/source given below and answer the questions that follow:

"A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side."

Read the passage above and answer the following questions:
Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.
questions.markingScheme:
[1 Mark] v = 30 cm with formula
[1 Mark] m = -1 calculation
[2 Marks] Full image formed with explanation of reduced brightness due to half light intensity

questions.questionText:
(a) State the principle of a moving coil galvanometer and derive the expression for current sensitivity.
(b) How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I? Derive the formula for required shunt resistance S.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Principle: A current carrying coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a deflecting torque τ = NIAB. In radial field, restoring torque Cθ = NIAB ⇒ θ = (NAB/C) I. Current sensitivity I_s = θ/I = NAB/C.
(b) By connecting a small low-value resistance (shunt S) in parallel with galvanometer coil. S = (I_g · G) / (I - I_g).

questions.questionText: Derive the expression for the fringe width (β) in Young's Double Slit Experiment.
questions.correctAnswer:
Path difference Δx = xd / D.
For nth bright fringe: x_n = n λ D / d.
Fringe width β = x_{n+1} - x_n = (n+1)λD/d - nλD/d = λD / d.

questions.questionText: Derive the expression for the torque experienced by an electric dipole of dipole moment p placed in a uniform electric field E.
questions.correctAnswer:
Force on +q is F₁ = qE along E; Force on -q is F₂ = -qE opposite to E. Net force = 0.
Torque τ = Force × perpendicular distance = qE × (2a sinθ) = (q · 2a) E sinθ = p E sinθ.
In vector notation: τ = p × E.

questions.questionText: State Gauss's Law in Electrostatics. Write its mathematical form.
questions.correctAnswer:
Gauss's law states that the total electric flux passing through any closed Gaussian surface in vacuum is equal to 1/ε₀ times the net electric charge enclosed by that surface.
∮ E · dA = q_enclosed / ε₀.

questions.questionText: Derive the relation between drift velocity (v_d) of electrons and electric current (I) in a conductor of cross-sectional area A and electron density n.
questions.correctAnswer:
In time Δt, charge passing through area A: Δq = n · A · (v_d Δt) · e.
Current I = Δq / Δt = (n A v_d Δt e) / Δt = n e A v_d.
Therefore, I = n e A v_d.

questions.questionText: State Gauss's Law in Electrostatics and write its integral mathematical form for a closed surface enclosing charge q.
questions.correctAnswer:
Total electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface in vacuum is equal to q_enclosed / ε₀.
∮ E · dA = q / ε₀.

(b) A convex lens has focal length 20 cm in air. Find its focal length when immersed in water (μ_glass = 1.5, μ_water = 4/3).
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Refraction at surface 1: μ₂/v₁ - μ₁/u = (μ₂-μ₁)/R₁. Refraction at surface 2: μ₁/v - μ₂/v₁ = (μ₁-μ₂)/R₂. Adding both equations gives 1/v - 1/u = (μ - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). Since 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, 1/f = (μ - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂).
(b) 1/f_air = (1.5 - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = 0.5 K = 1/20 ⇒ K = 1/10. In water: 1/f_water = (1.5/(4/3) - 1) K = (9/8 - 1)(1/10) = (1/8)(1/10) = 1/80 ⇒ f_water = 80 cm.
questions.markingScheme:

questions.questionText: Using Crystal Field Theory (CFT), explain why [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic and outer orbital, whereas [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ is diamagnetic and inner orbital.
questions.correctAnswer:
Co³⁺ has 3d⁶ configuration.
In [CoF₆]³⁻, F⁻ is a weak field ligand (Δ_o < P), so pairing does not occur: t_{2g}⁴ e_g² with 4 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic, sp³d² outer orbital).
In [Co(CN)₆]³⁻, CN⁻ is a strong field ligand (Δ_o > P), so electrons pair up: t_{2g}⁶ e_g⁰ with 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic, d²sp³ inner orbital).

(a) 1st Law: Mass of substance deposited m = Z · I · t = Z Q.
2nd Law: When same quantity of electricity passes through different electrolytes, masses deposited are proportional to their chemical equivalent weights (m₁/E₁ = m₂/E₂).
(b) E°_cell = E°_cathode - E°_anode = 0.34 - (-2.37) = +2.71 V.

ΔG° = -n F E°_cell = -2 × 96500 × 2.71 = -523.03 kJ/mol.

questions.questionText: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeros are (3 + √5) and (3 - √5).

Product of zeros (P) = (3 + √5)(3 - √5) = 3² - (√5)² = 9 - 5 = 4.
Required polynomial p(x) = k(x² - Sx + P) = k(x² - 6x + 4).

questions.questionText: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin θ - 2 sin³ θ) / (2 cos³ θ - cos θ) = tan θ.
questions.correctAnswer:
LHS = [sin θ (1 - 2 sin² θ)] / [cos θ (2 cos² θ - 1)].
Since 1 - 2 sin² θ = cos 2θ and 2 cos² θ - 1 = cos 2θ (or replacing 1 = sin² θ + cos² θ), numerator and denominator brackets cancel out: sin θ / cos θ = tan θ = RHS.

Q3. Find the volume of the hemisphere attached at the top. (1M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Radius r = 4.2/2 = 2.1 cm. CSA of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × (2.1)² = 27.72 cm².
Q2. TSA of block = TSA of cube - Base area of hemisphere + CSA of hemisphere
= 6a² - πr² + 2πr² = 6(5)² + πr² = 150 + (22/7) × (2.1)² = 150 + 13.86 = 163.86 cm².
Q3. Volume = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × (2.1)³ = 19.404 cm³.

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

questions.questionText:

1. Private Final Consumption Expenditure = ₹ 1,200 Cr
2. Government Final Consumption Expenditure = ₹ 400 Cr
3. Gross Domestic Capital Formation = ₹ 300 Cr
4. Net Exports = (-) ₹ 50 Cr
5. Depreciation = ₹ 40 Cr
6. Net Indirect Taxes = ₹ 100 Cr
7. Net Factor Income from Abroad = ₹ 20 Cr
questions.correctAnswer:

GDP_MP = Private Exp + Govt Exp + Gross Cap Formation + Net Exports

NDP_FC = NDP_MP - Net Indirect Taxes = 1810 - 100 = ₹ 1,710 Cr.
NNP_FC (National Income) = NDP_FC + NFIA = 1710 + 20 = ₹ 1,730 Cr.

questions.questionText: Explain the working of Money Multiplier with a numerical example assuming Initial Deposit = ₹ 1,000 and LRR = 20%.

Money Multiplier = 1 / LRR = 1 / 0.20 = 5 times.
Initial Deposit of ₹ 1,000 creates total money supply = Initial Deposit × Money Multiplier = ₹ 1,000 × 5 = ₹ 5,000.
Banks keep ₹ 200 (20%) as reserve and lend ₹ 800 in Round 1, generating secondary deposits until total credit reaches ₹ 5,000.

questions.questionText: Explain the mechanism of Income Determination where Aggregate Demand equals Aggregate Supply (AD = AS). What happens when AD > AS or AD < AS?
questions.correctAnswer:
Equilibrium occurs at point where AD = C + I equals AS = Y.
1. When AD > AS: Consumers buy more than producers produce. Inventories fall below desired level. Firms increase production and employment until AD = AS.
2. When AD < AS: Unsold stock accumulates. Producers cut production and employment until inventory normalizes and AD = AS.

questions.questionText: What is decentralisation? Describe the major steps taken in 1992 towards decentralisation in India through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments.

1. Mandatory regular elections to local government bodies.
2. Reservation of seats for SC, ST, and OBC communities.
3. At least one-third (33%) of all positions reserved for women.
4. Creation of an independent State Election Commission in each state.
5. State governments required to share powers and revenue with local bodies.

2. Over seven years, three wars were fought against Denmark, Austria, and France, ending in Prussian victory.

questions.questionText: An object 4 cm tall is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, nature, and size of the image formed.

questions.questionText:
A circuit consists of three resistors R1 = 5 Ω, R2 = 10 Ω, and R3 = 30 Ω connected in parallel across a 12 V battery.
(a) Draw the circuit diagram showing a switch, ammeter, and voltmeter.
(b) Calculate the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination.
(c) Calculate the total current flowing in the circuit.
(d) Calculate the current flowing through each individual resistor.
questions.markingScheme:
[1 mark] Correct circuit diagram with proper polarities
[1.5 marks] Rp calculation with steps
[1 mark] Total current calculation
[1.5 marks] Individual currents I1, I2, I3

questions.questionText:
(a) State Ohm's Law. Write its mathematical expression and specify conditions under which it holds valid.
(b) Draw a schematic circuit diagram to verify Ohm's law with battery, ammeter, voltmeter, rheostat, and test resistor.
(c) A wire of resistance 20 Ω is drawn out so that its length is increased to twice its original length. Calculate the new resistance of the wire.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) V ∝ I at constant temperature (V = IR).
(b) Circuit shows DC source, plug key, rheostat, resistor with voltmeter in parallel and ammeter in series.
(c) When length doubles (L' = 2L), cross-sectional area halves (A' = A/2) since volume is constant. New Resistance R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4 × 20 = 80 Ω.

questions.questionText:
(a) Describe double circulation in the human heart with a schematic flow diagram.
(b) Why is double circulation advantageous in birds and mammals?
(c) Distinguish between arteries and veins based on wall thickness, direction of flow, and internal valves.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Blood flows through heart twice in one complete cycle: Pulmonary circulation (Heart → Lungs → Heart) and Systemic circulation (Heart → Body tissues → Heart).
(b) Completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, providing efficient oxygen delivery needed for high metabolic rates and body temperature regulation.
(c) Arteries: Thick elastic walls, carry blood away from heart, no valves. Veins: Thin walls, carry blood towards heart, have valves.

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side.
questions.questionText:
Read the passage above and answer the following questions:
Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.
questions.markingScheme:
[1 Mark] v = 30 cm with formula
[1 Mark] m = -1 calculation
[2 Marks] Full image formed with explanation of reduced brightness due to half light intensity

questions.questionText: State two differences between acquired traits and inherited traits with one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited traits are caused by changes in DNA/germ cells and passed to offspring (e.g., eye color). Acquired traits develop during lifetime and cannot be passed on (e.g., muscle building, scar).

generalInstructions: This question paper contains questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. Internal choices are provided in 2 questions of Section C, all questions of Section D, and 1 question of Section E.
Section A comprises Objective Type questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 120 to 150 words.
Section E comprises Case-Based / Source-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts (i), (ii), and (iii).
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat, properly labeled diagrams and step-wise calculations should be shown.

questions.casePassage: Gregor Mendel conducted pioneering hybridization experiments on garden pea plants (Pisum sativum). He crossed a pure-breeding round and yellow-seeded pea plant (RRYY) with a pure-breeding wrinkled and green-seeded pea plant (rryy). In the F1 generation, all offspring had round and yellow seeds. The F1 generation plants were then self-pollinated to produce the F2 generation.
questions.questionText:
Read the passage/source given below and answer the questions that follow:

"Gregor Mendel conducted pioneering hybridization experiments on garden pea plants (Pisum sativum). He crossed a pure-breeding round and yellow-seeded pea plant (RRYY) with a pure-breeding wrinkled and green-seeded pea plant (rryy). In the F1 generation, all offspring had round and yellow seeds. The F1 generation plants were then self-pollinated to produce the F2 generation."

Q1. What is the genotype and phenotype of the F1 generation plants? (1M)
Q2. State Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment demonstrated by this dihybrid cross. (1M)
Q3. State the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation. If 1600 plants are obtained in F2, calculate the expected number of plants with round and green seeds. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Genotype: RrYy; Phenotype: Round and Yellow seeds.
Q2. When two pairs of contrasting traits are combined in a hybrid, segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair during gamete formation.
Q3. Phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1 (Round-Yellow : Round-Green : Wrinkled-Yellow : Wrinkled-Green). Expected Round-Green = (3/16) × 1600 = 300 plants.

questions.correctAnswer: Ethane shows single covalent C-C and C-H bonds with 7 electron pairs. N2 shows a triple covalent bond sharing 3 electron pairs between two nitrogen atoms (:N≡N:).

questions.questionText:
Read the case study / contextual scenario given below and answer the following sub-questions:

State two differences between acquired traits and inherited traits with one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited traits are caused by changes in DNA/germ cells and passed to offspring (e.g., eye color). Acquired traits develop during lifetime and cannot be passed on (e.g., muscle building, scar).

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

questions.correctAnswer: कैप्टन एक साधारण, बूढ़ा और दिव्यांग फेरीवाला था, लेकिन उसके मन में स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों और विशेषकर नेताजी सुभाषचंद्र बोस के प्रति अगाध श्रद्धा और देशप्रेम की प्रबल भावना थी। वह नेताजी की बिना चश्मे वाली मूर्ति को अधूरा मानकर अपनी ओर से चश्मा लगाता था। उसकी इसी सच्ची देशभक्ति और आदर भावना के कारण लोग उसे आदर से ‘कैप्टन’ कहते थे।

questions.correctAnswer: गोपियाँ उद्धव को 'बड़भागी' कहकर उन पर कटाक्ष करती हैं। वे कहती हैं कि तुम कृष्ण के सानिध्य में रहकर भी प्रेम के बंधन से मुक्त हो, जो एक विडंबना है।

questions.questionText: हालदार साहब के माध्यम से लेखक ने देशभक्ति की किस नई परिभाषा को प्रस्तुत किया है?
questions.correctAnswer: हालदार साहब एक संवेदनशील नागरिक हैं। वे चश्मे वाले की देशभक्ति का सम्मान करते हैं। लेखक ने स्पष्ट किया है कि देशभक्ति केवल बड़े कार्यों में नहीं, बल्कि छोटे-छोटे प्रयासों में भी निहित है।

questions.questionText: ‘सेनानी न होते हुए भी चश्मेवाले को लोग कैप्टन क्यों कहते थे?’ पाठ के आधार पर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.correctAnswer: कैप्टन के हृदय में स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों व देश के शहीदों के प्रति अगाध श्रद्धा थी। नेताजी की बिना चश्मे वाली मूर्ति देखकर उसे आहत होता था, इसलिए लोग उसे आदर से कैप्टन कहते थे।

questions.casePassage: ‘मूर्ति संगमरमर की थी। टोपी की नोक से कोट के दूसरे बटन तक कोई दो फुट ऊँची। जिसे कहते हैं बस्ट; और सुंदर थी। नेताजी सुंदर लग रहे थे। कुछ-कुछ मासूम और कमसिन। फौजी वर्दी में। मूर्ति को देखते ही ‘दिल्ली चलो’ और ‘तुम मुझे खून दो...’ वगैरह याद आने लगते थे। केवल एक चीज़ की कसर थी—नेताजी की आँखों पर चश्मा नहीं था।’

Q3. मूर्ति में किस मुख्य बात की कमी थी और उसे कौन पूरा करता था? (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:

Q3. मूर्ति पर संगमरमर का चश्मा नहीं था, जिसे देशभक्त कैप्टन चश्मेवाला सचमुच का चश्मा पहनाकर पूरा करता था।

generalInstructions: This question paper contains 39 questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. However, internal choices have been provided in some questions.
Section A comprises 20 objective questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises 6 Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises 7 Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises 3 Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 80 to 120 words.
Section E comprises 3 Case-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts.
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat and properly labeled diagrams/calculations should be shown.

questions.questionText:
(a) What is a homologous series? List three main characteristics of carbon homologous series.
(b) Give the chemical formula, electron dot structure, and IUPAC name of the 3rd member of the alkane series.
(c) Explain with balanced chemical equations:
 (i) Esterification reaction
 (ii) Saponification reaction.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) A family of organic compounds with same functional group where successive members differ by -CH2 unit and 14 u mass.
(b) Propane (C3H8), CH3-CH2-CH3.
(c) (i) CH3COOH + C2H5OH --(conc. H2SO4)--> CH3COOC2H5 (Ethyl ethanoate) + H2O.
(ii) CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH.

questions.questionText: What is an amphoteric oxide? Give two balanced chemical equations showing aluminum oxide reacting with an acid and a base.
questions.correctAnswer:
Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases to produce salt and water.
(i) Al2O3 + 6HCl → 2AlCl3 + 3H2O
(ii) Al2O3 + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO2 (Sodium Aluminate) + H2O.

questions.questionText: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Write the overall balanced chemical equation for cellular respiration.
questions.correctAnswer:
Respiration breaks down glucose in the presence of oxygen, releasing ATP thermal energy.
Equation: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + Energy (ATP).

questions.questionText: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration on the basis of: (i) Location in cell (ii) End products formed.
questions.correctAnswer:
(i) Aerobic: Mitochondria & cytoplasm; Anaerobic: Cytoplasm only.
(ii) Aerobic end products: CO2 + H2O + 36/38 ATP; Anaerobic (in yeast): Ethanol + CO2 + 2 ATP (or Lactic acid in muscles).

questions.questionText:
(a) Give reasons why ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
(b) Explain why ionic solids do not conduct electricity in solid state but conduct well in aqueous solution or molten state.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions require large thermal energy to break.
(b) In solid state, ions are locked in rigid crystal lattice. In aqueous/molten state, ions are free to move and conduct charge.

questions.questionText: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Bromine

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Decomposition of calcium carbonate into quicklime and carbon dioxide is an endothermic reaction.
Reason (R): Endothermic reactions absorb thermal energy from the surroundings to break chemical bonds.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition of CaCO3 requires heat energy (absorbs heat), so it is endothermic.

questions.questionText: The breakdown of pyruvate into carbon dioxide, water, and ATP energy in the presence of oxygen occurs in:
questions.correctAnswer: A) Mitochondria

questions.questionText: A ray of light traveling in water falls obliquely on a glass plate. Does the light ray bend towards or away from the normal? State reason based on optical density.
questions.correctAnswer: Refractive index of glass (1.5) is greater than water (1.33). As light passes from a rarer to a denser medium, it slows down and bends towards the normal.

questions.questionText: When aqueous solutions of potassium iodide and lead nitrate are mixed, an insoluble yellow precipitate is formed. What is the chemical formula of the yellow precipitate?
questions.correctAnswer: B) PbI2

questions.questionText:
(a) Draw a neat labeled diagram of a reflex arc showing receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, and effector organ.
(b) Why are reflex actions routed through the spinal cord rather than brain processing?
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Receptor (skin) → Sensory Neuron → Relay Neuron in Spinal Cord → Motor Neuron → Effector (muscle contraction).
(b) Spinal reflexes provide instant, life-saving responses to danger without delay of conscious brain evaluation.

questions.questionText: Depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer is primarily caused by synthetic chemicals known as:

questions.questionText: An object 4 cm tall is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, nature, and size of the image formed.
questions.correctAnswer:
u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm.
1/v + 1/u = 1/f => 1/v = -1/15 - (-1/20) = -1/60 => v = -60 cm.
Nature: Real, inverted, in front of mirror.
Magnification m = -v/u = -(-60)/(-20) = -3. Height h' = m × h = -3 × 4 = -12 cm (magnified).

questions.questionText: Why does the clear sky appear blue during the daytime, but deep dark black to an astronaut in outer space?
questions.correctAnswer: Air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than red (Rayleigh scattering). In outer space, there is no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, so the sky appears dark.

questions.questionText: A 100 W electric bulb operates for 10 hours daily. Calculate the electrical energy consumed in kWh units over a period of 30 days.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy = Power × Time = (100/1000 kW) × 10 h × 30 days = 0.1 × 300 = 30 kWh (units).

questions.questionText: How does binary fission in Amoeba differ from multiple fission in Plasmodium?
questions.correctAnswer: Binary fission divides one parent cell into two daughter cells under favorable conditions. Multiple fission divides one cell into many daughter cells simultaneously within a protective cyst.

(b) Why should POP be stored in a completely moisture-proof container? Write the reaction.
questions.correctAnswer:

questions.questionText:
(a) Define Electric Power. Write three different mathematical formulas for electric power in terms of V, I, and R.
(b) An electric heater of resistance 8 Ω draws 15 A from the service mains for 2 hours. Calculate the rate at which heat is developed in the heater.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Rate of doing electrical work. P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
(b) Rate of heat development = Power P = I²R = (15)² × 8 = 225 × 8 = 1800 Joules/second (Watts).

questions.questionText: Which of the following observations is correct when aqueous potassium iodide reacts with lead nitrate?

B) Evolution of a pungent gas

sections.description: Long Answer Questions with Stepwise Evaluation (3 Questions = 12 Marks)

questions.questionText:
(a) Describe double circulation in the human heart with a schematic flow diagram.
(b) Why is double circulation advantageous in birds and mammals?
(c) Distinguish between arteries and veins based on wall thickness, direction of flow, and internal valves.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Blood flows through heart twice in one complete cycle: Pulmonary circulation (Heart → Lungs → Heart) and Systemic circulation (Heart → Body tissues → Heart).
(b) Completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, providing efficient oxygen delivery needed for high metabolic rates and body temperature regulation.
(c) Arteries: Thick elastic walls, carry blood away from heart, no valves. Veins: Thin walls, carry blood towards heart, have valves.

questions.questionText: Vegetative propagation in Bryophyllum occurs through:

questions.questionText: The self-linking ability of carbon atoms through covalent bonds is called:

questions.questionText: State two differences between acquired traits and inherited traits with one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited traits are caused by changes in DNA/germ cells and passed to offspring (e.g., eye color). Acquired traits develop during lifetime and cannot be passed on (e.g., muscle building, scar).

questions.casePassage: A domestic electric circuit is supplied with 220 V alternating current (AC) with a 50 Hz frequency. In an urban household, appliances such as an electric iron (1100 W), a refrigerator (400 W), four LED bulbs (25 W each), and a television (100 W) are connected across a 15 A power line through safety devices including an MCB and earth wire.
questions.questionText:
Q1. Why are domestic electrical appliances connected in parallel combination rather than series? (1M)
Q2. Calculate the total electric current drawn when all the above appliances operate simultaneously on 220 V. (2M)
Q3. State the primary safety function of an electric fuse / MCB in a domestic circuit. (1M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Parallel combination ensures each appliance receives full 220 V, operates independently with its own switch, and if one appliance fails, others continue working.
Q2. Total Power P = 1100 + 400 + (4 × 25) + 100 = 1700 W. Total Current I = P/V = 1700 / 220 = 7.73 A.
Q3. Protects circuit from overloading and short-circuits by breaking the circuit when current exceeds safe rating.

questions.correctAnswer: A) Yellow, PbI2

questions.questionText: How does binary fission in Amoeba differ from multiple fission in Plasmodium?

sections.description: Short Answer Questions (2 Questions carrying 3 Marks each = 4 Marks)

questions.questionText:
(a) Describe double circulation in the human heart with a schematic flow diagram.
(b) Why is double circulation advantageous in birds and mammals?
(c) Distinguish between arteries and veins based on wall thickness, direction of flow, and internal valves.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Blood flows through heart twice in one complete cycle: Pulmonary circulation (Heart → Lungs → Heart) and Systemic circulation (Heart → Body tissues → Heart).
(b) Completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, providing efficient oxygen delivery needed for high metabolic rates and body temperature regulation.
(c) Arteries: Thick elastic walls, carry blood away from heart, no valves. Veins: Thin walls, carry blood towards heart, have valves.

questions.questionText: What is biological magnification (biomagnification)? Name the trophic level that accumulates the highest concentration of toxic chemicals.

generalInstructions: This question paper contains questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. Internal choices are provided in 2 questions of Section C, all questions of Section D, and 1 question of Section E.
Section A comprises Objective Type questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 120 to 150 words.
Section E comprises Case-Based / Source-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts (i), (ii), and (iii).
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat, properly labeled diagrams and step-wise calculations should be shown.

generalInstructions: The question paper consists of 37 questions in 5 sections.
Section A: Questions 1 to 20 are MCQs of 1 mark each.
Section B: Questions 21 to 26 are Very Short Answer type of 2 marks each.
Section C: Questions 27 to 33 are Short Answer type of 3 marks each.
Section D: Questions 34 to 36 are Long Answer type of 5 marks each.
Section E: Questions 37 to 39 are Case-Based questions of 4 marks each.

questions.questionText: Which of the following treaties recognized Greece as an independent nation in 1832?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Treaty of Constantinople

questions.questionText: Assertion (A): Resources are vital for human survival and maintaining quality of life. Reason (R): Human beings used resources indiscriminately, leading to major ecological crises.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.questionText: 'Democracy is seen to be good in principle, but felt to be not so good in its practice.' Critically evaluate this statement.
questions.correctAnswer:
In Principle: Democracy promotes equality, enhances individual dignity, improves decision quality, and provides peaceful mechanisms to resolve social conflicts.
In Practice: Democracies often appear slow due to deliberative procedures, suffer from corruption, and do not eliminate poverty overnight.
Conclusion: Democracy is an enabling political framework that creates conditions for citizens to achieve goals, making it superior to any alternative regime.

questions.questionText: Rabi crops in India are sown in:
questions.correctAnswer: A) October to December (Winter)

questions.questionText: Solve the following problem regarding various institutional and technological reforms introduced by the Government of India in the agricultural sector after independence.
questions.correctAnswer:
Institutional Reforms:
1. Collectivization, consolidation of land holdings, and abolition of the Zamindari system.
2. Provision of crop insurance against drought, flood, cyclone, fire, and diseases.
3. Establishment of Grameen banks, cooperative societies, and Kisan Credit Card (KCC).
Technological Reforms:
4. Green Revolution using HYV seeds and chemical fertilizers, and White Revolution (Operation Flood).
5. Special weather bulletins and agricultural programs broadcast over radio and television.

questions.questionText: Distinguish between 'Coming Together' and 'Holding Together' federations with one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer:
Coming Together: Independent states come together on their own to form a bigger unit to pool sovereignty and retain identity (e.g., USA, Australia).
Holding Together: A large country divides its power between constituent states and the national government (e.g., India, Spain).

questions.questionText: Explain the significance of the 'Khilafat Movement' in the context of the Non-Cooperation movement.
questions.correctAnswer: The Khilafat issue allowed Gandhi to unite Hindus and Muslims; it brought Muslims into the national struggle against British rule; it provided a platform for a unified mass movement.
questions.markingScheme: 1 mark for each valid point (3 points required).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Solar Energy

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between Prudential and Moral reasons for power sharing with suitable examples.
questions.correctAnswer:
Prudential Reasons: Based on careful calculation of gains and losses. Power sharing reduces the possibility of social conflict and ensures political stability (e.g., reserving seats for minority communities in Belgium).
Moral Reasons: Based on the intrinsic value of democracy. Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy where citizens have a right to be consulted on how they are governed.
questions.markingScheme:
[1.5 marks] Prudential reasons definition and example
[1.5 marks] Moral reasons definition and example

questions.questionText: Why is credit considered to have a 'double-edged' impact on borrowers? Explain with contrasting examples.
questions.correctAnswer:
Positive impact: Credit enables profitable investment in farming/business, increasing earnings (e.g., Salim expanding shoe production).
Negative impact (Debt Trap): If crops fail due to natural disasters, repayment becomes impossible, forcing the borrower to sell land (e.g., Swapna's crop failure).

questions.markingScheme: [2 Mark(s)] Full credit awarded for correct conceptual reasoning and steps.

questions.casePassage: Suppose a country has four families. The average per capita income of these families is ₹5000. If the income of three families is ₹4000, ₹7000, and ₹3000 respectively, answer the following:
questions.questionText:
Q1. What is the income of the fourth family? (1M)
Q2. Why is Average Income (Per Capita Income) considered an insufficient measure to compare development between two countries? Give two reasons. (2M)
Q3. Name the index published by UNDP that provides a comprehensive measure of development beyond mere income. (1M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Total income = 4 × 5000 = ₹20,000. Fourth family income = 20000 - (4000 + 7000 + 3000) = 20000 - 14000 = ₹6000.
Q2. Per Capita Income hides disparities. It does not tell us how income is distributed among people, nor does it account for health, education, and gender equality.
Q3. Human Development Index (HDI).
questions.markingScheme:
[1 mark] Q1 Calculation ₹6000
[2 marks] Q2 Two valid limitations of Per Capita Income
[1 mark] Q3 Human Development Index (HDI)

questions.questionText: What is decentralisation? Describe the major steps taken in 1992 towards decentralisation in India through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments.
questions.correctAnswer:
Decentralisation means taking power away from Central and State governments and giving it to local government.
Major Steps in 1992:
1. Mandatory regular elections to local government bodies.
2. Reservation of seats for SC, ST, and OBC communities.
3. At least one-third (33%) of all positions reserved for women.
4. Creation of an independent State Election Commission in each state.
5. State governments required to share powers and revenue with local bodies.

 (i) Esterification reaction
 (ii) Saponification reaction.
questions.correctAnswer:

(b) Propane (C3H8), CH3-CH2-CH3.
(c) (i) CH3COOH + C2H5OH --(conc. H2SO4)--> CH3COOC2H5 (Ethyl ethanoate) + H2O.

questions.questionText: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Write the overall balanced chemical equation for cellular respiration.
questions.correctAnswer:
Respiration breaks down glucose in the presence of oxygen, releasing ATP thermal energy.
Equation: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + Energy (ATP).

questions.questionText: When aqueous solutions of potassium iodide and lead nitrate are mixed, an insoluble yellow precipitate is formed. What is the chemical formula of the yellow precipitate?
questions.correctAnswer: B) PbI2

questions.questionText: Which gas is evolved when iron filings react with steam?
questions.correctAnswer: Hydrogen

questions.questionText:
(a) What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris (POP)? How is it prepared from Gypsum?
(b) Why should POP be stored in a completely moisture-proof container? Write the reaction.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) CaSO4·1/2H2O. Prepared by heating Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) at 373 K (100°C).
(b) On contact with water, it rehydrates into a hard solid mass (Gypsum): CaSO4·1/2H2O + 1.5H2O → CaSO4·2H2O.

questions.questionText:
(a) Draw a neat labeled diagram of a reflex arc showing receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron, and effector organ.
(b) Why are reflex actions routed through the spinal cord rather than brain processing?
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Receptor (skin) → Sensory Neuron → Relay Neuron in Spinal Cord → Motor Neuron → Effector (muscle contraction).
(b) Spinal reflexes provide instant, life-saving responses to danger without delay of conscious brain evaluation.

questions.questionText: 1. What is the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation? 2. Why did the short trait disappear in F1 but reappear in F2?

questions.questionText: State two distinct properties of magnetic field lines around a straight bar magnet.
questions.correctAnswer:

questions.questionText: Why does the clear sky appear blue during the daytime, but deep dark black to an astronaut in outer space?
questions.correctAnswer: Air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than red (Rayleigh scattering). In outer space, there is no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, so the sky appears dark.

questions.questionText: Which metal is stored in kerosene oil to prevent accidental fire?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Sodium

questions.questionText: A 100 W electric bulb operates for 10 hours daily. Calculate the electrical energy consumed in kWh units over a period of 30 days.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy = Power × Time = (100/1000 kW) × 10 h × 30 days = 0.1 × 300 = 30 kWh (units).

questions.questionText: A 4 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. The distance of the object from the lens is 15 cm. Find the nature, position, and size of the image formed.
questions.correctAnswer: Using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f; 1/v - 1/(-15) = 1/20 => v = -60cm [1.5 marks]. Magnification m = v/u = -60/-15 = +4. Size = 4 * 4 = 16 cm [1.5 marks]. Virtual and erect.
questions.markingScheme: 1.5 marks for lens formula application, 1.5 marks for magnification and size calculation.

questions.correctAnswer: A) Yellow, PbI2

questions.correctAnswer: A) Catenation

questions.questionText: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the cable tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.correctAnswer:
Let building AB = 7 m and tower CE = h m.
In △ABD (where D is foot of tower): tan 45° = AB / BD => 1 = 7 / BD => BD = 7 m.
Therefore horizontal distance to tower AE = BD = 7 m.
In △CAE: tan 60° = CE / AE => √3 = CE / 7 => CE = 7√3 m.
Total height of tower = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(√3 + 1) = 7(1.732 + 1) = 7 × 2.732 = 19.124 m.

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

Q3. Calculate the power of this convex lens in Dioptres. If it is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 50 cm, find the net power of the combination. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side.
questions.questionText:

Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.

(a) Describe the structure of human female embryo sac (megagametophyte) with a neat labelled diagram.
(b) Solve the following problem regarding outbreeding devices developed by flowering plants to prevent self-pollination.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Mature embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate: 3 antipodal cells at chalazal end, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei, and egg apparatus at micropylar end (1 egg cell + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus).
(b) Outbreeding devices: 1. Dichogamy (pollen release and stigma receptivity not synchronized), 2. Heterostyly/Herkogamy (anther and stigma placed at different positions), 3. Self-incompatibility (genetic prevention of self-pollen germination), 4. Dioecy (unisexual male and female plants).

questions.questionText: Solve the following problem regarding semi-conservative mode of DNA replication with reference to the Meselson and Stahl experiment.
questions.correctAnswer:
Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium for generations, then transferred them to ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium.
Generation 1 (20 min) yielded hybrid DNA (¹⁴N-¹⁵N) of intermediate density in CsCl gradient.
Generation 2 (40 min) yielded equal amounts of light (¹⁴N-¹⁴N) and hybrid DNA, proving each daughter DNA molecule conserves one parental strand and synthesizes one new strand.

questions.questionText: State Chargaff's rule for double-stranded DNA structure.
questions.correctAnswer: In any double-stranded DNA, the amount of Adenine is always equal to Thymine (A = T), and Guanine equals Cytosine (G = C). Therefore, Purines = Pyrimidines (A + G = T + C).

questions.questionText: Solve the following problem regarding steps involved in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) with suitable temperatures.
questions.correctAnswer:
1. Denaturation (94-96 °C): Double-stranded target DNA separates into two single strands.
2. Annealing (50-60 °C): Two sets of oligonucleotide primers bind to complementary regions.
3. Extension (72 °C): Thermostable Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands using dNTPs.

questions.questionText: Describe the lac operon model in Escherichia coli in the presence and absence of lactose.
questions.correctAnswer:
In absence of lactose (switch OFF): Lac repressor protein synthesized by i-gene binds to the operator (o) region, preventing RNA polymerase from transcribing structural genes (z, y, a).
In presence of lactose (inducer, switch ON): Lactose binds repressor protein, inactivating it. RNA polymerase transcribes lac z (β-galactosidase), lac y (permease), and lac a (transacetylase).

questions.questionText: Explain the semi-conservative mode of DNA replication with reference to the Meselson and Stahl experiment.

Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium for generations, then transferred them to ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium.

questions.questionText:
(a) Describe the structure of human female embryo sac (megagametophyte) with a neat labelled diagram.
(b) Explain the outbreeding devices developed by flowering plants to prevent self-pollination.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Mature embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate: 3 antipodal cells at chalazal end, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei, and egg apparatus at micropylar end (1 egg cell + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus).
(b) Outbreeding devices: 1. Dichogamy (pollen release and stigma receptivity not synchronized), 2. Heterostyly/Herkogamy (anther and stigma placed at different positions), 3. Self-incompatibility (genetic prevention of self-pollen germination), 4. Dioecy (unisexual male and female plants).

generalInstructions: This question paper contains questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. Internal choices are provided in 2 questions of Section C, all questions of Section D, and 1 question of Section E.
Section A comprises Objective Type questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 120 to 150 words.
Section E comprises Case-Based / Source-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts (i), (ii), and (iii).
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat, properly labeled diagrams and step-wise calculations should be shown.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the cable tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.correctAnswer:
Let building AB = 7 m and tower CE = h m.
In △ABD (where D is foot of tower): tan 45° = AB / BD => 1 = 7 / BD => BD = 7 m.
Therefore horizontal distance to tower AE = BD = 7 m.
In △CAE: tan 60° = CE / AE => √3 = CE / 7 => CE = 7√3 m.
Total height of tower = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(√3 + 1) = 7(1.732 + 1) = 7 × 2.732 = 19.124 m.

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

sections.description: Unseen Passages and Analytical Comprehension

questions.questionText: Based on the passage, why is 'deep work' considered a 'rare superpower' in the current professional landscape?
options: A) Because it is a technological innovation.
B) Because modern tools hinder sustained concentration.
C) Because it requires expensive software.
D) Because it is only for students.
questions.correctAnswer: B) Because modern tools hinder sustained concentration.
questions.markingScheme: 1 mark for correct identification of the central idea.
questions.casePassage: In the digital age, the concept of 'deep work'—the ability to focus without distraction on a cognitively demanding task—is becoming a rare superpower. As modern communication tools fragment our attention, the capacity to stay immersed in complex problem solving determines one's professional success. Studies show that a single notification can derail focus for up to twenty minutes.

questions.questionText:
SECTION B: CREATIVE WRITING SKILLS - ANALYTICAL PARAGRAPH (5 MARKS)

The chart below displays the preferred learning resources used by Class 10 students for Board Examination preparation in 2024-2025:
• Interactive AI Mock Tests & Question Banks: 45%
• Textbooks & Official Exemplar Solutions: 30%
• Offline Coaching & Tuition Notes: 15%
• Peer Study Groups: 10%

Write an Analytical Paragraph (100–120 words) analyzing the data provided. Compare trends, highlight key findings, and draw a meaningful conclusion.
questions.correctAnswer:
Structure:
- Introduction (Restate chart topic in own words).
- Body Paragraph (Compare 45% AI mock tests vs 30% traditional textbooks vs 15% coaching notes and 10% group study).
- Conclusion (Synthesize that digital self-paced evaluation is leading board prep trends while core textbooks remain fundamental).
questions.markingScheme:
[1 Mark] Introductory thesis statement
[2 Marks] Comparative analysis of statistics and trends
[2 Marks] Cohesion, clarity, grammatical accuracy and concluding summary

questions.chapterName: First Flight: Nelson Mandela - Long Walk to Freedom
questions.questionText: What according to Nelson Mandela are the "twin obligations" every man has in life? Why was it impossible for a man of his birth and colour to fulfill both obligations in South Africa under Apartheid?
questions.correctAnswer:
Twin Obligations:
1. Obligation to family, parents, wife, and children.
2. Obligation to his people, community, and country.
Under Apartheid rule, a person of colour in South Africa who tried to fulfill his duty to his people was inevitably ripped from his family, isolated, and forced to live an existence of secrecy and rebellion as a freedom fighter.
questions.markingScheme:
[2 Marks] Clearly stating the two obligations
[3 Marks] Analyzing the historical constraint under Apartheid policy

questions.questionText: Analyze Lencho’s reaction to receiving the money. Does it reflect blind faith or a sense of entitlement? Discuss with reference to 'A Letter to God'.

questions.markingScheme: 1 mark for identifying the trait, 2 marks for analysis, 2 marks for textual evidence [5 marks total].
questions.casePassage: Lencho showed not the slightest surprise on seeing the money; such was his confidence—but he became angry when he counted the money. God could not have made a mistake, nor could he have denied Lencho what he had requested.

questions.correctAnswer: The Buddha asks Kisa Gotami to bring a handful of mustard seeds from a household where no child, husband, parent, or friend has ever died. When she finds no such house, she realizes that grief is universal and death is the common destiny of all mortals.

generalInstructions: This question paper contains 39 questions divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
All questions are compulsory. However, internal choices have been provided in some questions.
Section A comprises 20 objective questions (MCQs and Assertion-Reasoning) carrying 1 mark each.
Section B comprises 6 Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each. Answers should be within 30 to 50 words.
Section C comprises 7 Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each. Answers should be within 50 to 80 words.
Section D comprises 3 Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each. Answers should be within 80 to 120 words.
Section E comprises 3 Case-Based integrated units of assessment carrying 4 marks each with sub-parts.
There is no overall choice. Wherever necessary, neat and properly labeled diagrams/calculations should be shown.

questions.questionText: An object 4 cm tall is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, nature, and size of the image formed.
questions.correctAnswer:
u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm.
1/v + 1/u = 1/f => 1/v = -1/15 - (-1/20) = -1/60 => v = -60 cm.
Nature: Real, inverted, in front of mirror.
Magnification m = -v/u = -(-60)/(-20) = -3. Height h' = m × h = -3 × 4 = -12 cm (magnified).

questions.questionText:
(a) Give reasons why ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
(b) Explain why ionic solids do not conduct electricity in solid state but conduct well in aqueous solution or molten state.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) Strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions require large thermal energy to break.
(b) In solid state, ions are locked in rigid crystal lattice. In aqueous/molten state, ions are free to move and conduct charge.

questions.questionText:

(b) Thermal: 2FeSO4 (s) → Fe2O3 (s) + SO2 (g) + SO3 (g)
Electrolytic: 2H2O (l) → 2H2 (g) + O2 (g).

questions.questionText: Why does the clear sky appear blue during the daytime, but deep dark black to an astronaut in outer space?
questions.correctAnswer: Air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than red (Rayleigh scattering). In outer space, there is no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, so the sky appears dark.

questions.questionText:

(b) Spinal reflexes provide instant, life-saving responses to danger without delay of conscious brain evaluation.

questions.questionText: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the cable tower. (Take √3 = 1.732)
questions.correctAnswer:
Let building AB = 7 m and tower CE = h m.
In △ABD (where D is foot of tower): tan 45° = AB / BD => 1 = 7 / BD => BD = 7 m.
Therefore horizontal distance to tower AE = BD = 7 m.
In △CAE: tan 60° = CE / AE => √3 = CE / 7 => CE = 7√3 m.
Total height of tower = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(√3 + 1) = 7(1.732 + 1) = 7 × 2.732 = 19.124 m.

[1 mark] Final height calculation = 19.12 m

questions.questionText: A motor boat whose speed is 18 km/h in still water takes 1 hour more to go 24 km upstream than to return downstream to the same spot. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.correctAnswer:
Let speed of stream = x km/h. Speed upstream = 18 - x, downstream = 18 + x.
24/(18 - x) - 24/(18 + x) = 1 => 24[18 + x - 18 + x] / (324 - x²) = 1 => 48x = 324 - x² => x² + 48x - 324 = 0 => (x + 54)(x - 6) = 0 => x = 6 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

Subtracting: -26x + 26y = -52 => -x + y = -2 => x - y = 2 (Eq 2).
Solving: x = 3, y = 1.

questions.casePassage: A decorative block shown in a handicraft museum is made of two solids — a cube and a hemisphere. The base of the block is a cube with edge 5 cm, and the hemisphere fixed on the top has a diameter of 4.2 cm. (Take π = 22/7)

questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Radius r = 4.2/2 = 2.1 cm. CSA of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × (2.1)² = 27.72 cm².
Q2. TSA of block = TSA of cube - Base area of hemisphere + CSA of hemisphere
= 6a² - πr² + 2πr² = 6(5)² + πr² = 150 + (22/7) × (2.1)² = 150 + 13.86 = 163.86 cm².
Q3. Volume = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × (2.1)³ = 19.404 cm³.
questions.markingScheme:

questions.questionText: Prove the trigonometric identity: (sin θ - 2 sin³ θ) / (2 cos³ θ - cos θ) = tan θ.
questions.correctAnswer:
LHS = [sin θ (1 - 2 sin² θ)] / [cos θ (2 cos² θ - 1)].
Since 1 - 2 sin² θ = cos 2θ and 2 cos² θ - 1 = cos 2θ (or replacing 1 = sin² θ + cos² θ), numerator and denominator brackets cancel out: sin θ / cos θ = tan θ = RHS.

questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): Decomposition of calcium carbonate into quicklime and carbon dioxide is an endothermic reaction.

options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.

Electrolytic: 2H2O (l) → 2H2 (g) + O2 (g).

(ii) Al2O3 + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO2 (Sodium Aluminate) + H2O.

questions.questionText:
(a) State Ohm's Law. Write its mathematical expression and specify conditions under which it holds valid.
(b) Draw a schematic circuit diagram to verify Ohm's law with battery, ammeter, voltmeter, rheostat, and test resistor.
(c) A wire of resistance 20 Ω is drawn out so that its length is increased to twice its original length. Calculate the new resistance of the wire.
questions.correctAnswer:
(a) V ∝ I at constant temperature (V = IR).
(b) Circuit shows DC source, plug key, rheostat, resistor with voltmeter in parallel and ammeter in series.
(c) When length doubles (L' = 2L), cross-sectional area halves (A' = A/2) since volume is constant. New Resistance R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4 × 20 = 80 Ω.

(b) Why is double circulation advantageous in birds and mammals?

questions.casePassage: A domestic electric circuit is supplied with 220 V alternating current (AC) with a 50 Hz frequency. In an urban household, appliances such as an electric iron (1100 W), a refrigerator (400 W), four LED bulbs (25 W each), and a television (100 W) are connected across a 15 A power line through safety devices including an MCB and earth wire.
questions.questionText:
Q1. Why are domestic electrical appliances connected in parallel combination rather than series? (1M)
Q2. Calculate the total electric current drawn when all the above appliances operate simultaneously on 220 V. (2M)
Q3. State the primary safety function of an electric fuse / MCB in a domestic circuit. (1M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Parallel combination ensures each appliance receives full 220 V, operates independently with its own switch, and if one appliance fails, others continue working.
Q2. Total Power P = 1100 + 400 + (4 × 25) + 100 = 1700 W. Total Current I = P/V = 1700 / 220 = 7.73 A.
Q3. Protects circuit from overloading and short-circuits by breaking the circuit when current exceeds safe rating.

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optics experiment in a laboratory using an optical bench. A luminous object is placed at different positions in front of a convex lens having a focal length of 20 cm. The positions of the object (u) and image (v) are measured accurately and tabulated.
questions.questionText:
Q1. If the object is placed at 40 cm in front of the lens, where will the image be formed? State its magnification. (1M)
Q2. What will be the nature of the image if the object is shifted to a distance of 15 cm from the lens? (1M)
Q3. Calculate the power of this convex lens in Dioptres. If it is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 50 cm, find the net power of the combination. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. At 2u = 2f = 40 cm on other side of lens (at 2F2). Magnification m = -1 (same size, real, inverted).
Q2. Virtual, erect, and magnified on same side as object (since u < f).
Q3. P1 = 100/20 = +5 D. P2 = 100/(-50) = -2 D. Net Power P = P1 + P2 = +5 - 2 = +3 D.

questions.casePassage: A student performs an optical bench experiment using a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A lighted candle is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens. A sharp real inverted image is captured on a white screen placed on the other side.
questions.questionText:
Read the passage above and answer the following questions:
Q1. At what distance from the lens will the sharp image be formed on the screen? (1M)
Q2. What is the magnification produced by the convex lens in this case? (1M)
Q3. If the top half of the convex lens is covered with a black paper, what change will be observed in the image formed on the screen? Give reasons. (2M)
questions.correctAnswer:
Q1. Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/15 = 1/v - 1/(-30) => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm on the other side.
Q2. Magnification m = v/u = (+30)/(-30) = -1.
Q3. A complete image will still be formed, but its intensity (brightness) will be reduced to half because fewer light rays pass through the uncovered half.
questions.markingScheme:
[1 Mark] v = 30 cm with formula
[1 Mark] m = -1 calculation
[2 Marks] Full image formed with explanation of reduced brightness due to half light intensity
